beats.text: A weekend job: ten thousand dollars more. The tax bracket says you keep eighty-six percent. The real number is closer to two thirds.
Kai's family earns fifty thousand, with two kids. The extra ten thousand gets hit three ways.
Federal tax first: fourteen percent, and the last fourteen hundred and seventy-seven dollars at twenty and a half. About fifteen hundred dollars.
Then the Canada Child Benefit. With two kids, it shrinks by thirteen and a half percent of the extra: thirteen hundred and fifty dollars.
And the groceries benefit drops five percent: another five hundred.
The twist: that's a third gone before provincial tax, CPP and EI. And the benefit cuts land the next July.
So before you say yes, count the benefits, not just the bracket.
Next: part-time or full-time, which pays more after benefits? Follow so you don't miss it.
